## Direct answer

HTTP version selection is not decided in the socket layer — it is threaded as a `version` value (`HTTP.VERSION_1` / `HTTP.VERSION_3`) from the CLI or `app.run()` down through `StartupMixin` into the worker function, and the actual fork happens in **`sanic/server/runners.py`** (`_serve_http_1` vs `_serve_http_3`) plus **`sanic/worker/serve.py::worker_serve()`**. The per-version implementation objects live in **`sanic/server/protocols/http_protocol.py`** (`HttpProtocol`, `Http3Protocol`), the enum in **`sanic/http/constants.py`**, and most runtime server configuration is supplied by **`sanic/mixins/startup.py`** (`run` / `prepare` / `_helper`) from `sanic/config.py` values.

## Stage 1 — where the version is chosen

`sanic/http/constants.py:22–30` @ `57d44f2` defines the only two supported versions:

```python
class HTTP(IntEnum):
    VERSION_1 = 1
    VERSION_3 = 3

    def display(self) -> str:
        value = 1.1 if self.value == 1 else self.value
        return f"HTTP/{value}"
```

`sanic/cli/arguments.py` (`HTTPVersionGroup`) exposes `--http 1|3` plus the shortcuts `-1` / `-3`; `prepare()` normalises the parsed values into `args.http = tuple(sorted(set(map(HTTP, args.http)), reverse=True))` — the reverse sort is deliberate, so HTTP/3 is prepared before HTTP/1.1 when both are requested.

`sanic/cli/app.py::SanicCLI.run()` then loops over that tuple:

```python
for http_version in self.args.http:
    app.prepare(**kwargs, version=http_version)
```

So a single process can pre-register more than one HTTP version (TCP HTTP/1.1 + UDP HTTP/3). Programmatic equivalent: `app.run(version=HTTP.VERSION_3)` — `version: HTTPVersion = HTTP.VERSION_1` is a keyword argument of both `StartupMixin.run()` and `StartupMixin.prepare()` in `sanic/mixins/startup.py`.

## Stage 2 — configuration decisions taken in `sanic/mixins/startup.py`

`prepare()` enforces the HTTP/3 deployment constraints and computes the deploy settings:

- **HTTP/3 must be first**: `if version == 3 and self.state.server_info: raise RuntimeError("Serving HTTP/3 instances as a secondary server is not supported. There can only be a single HTTP/3 worker and it must be the first instance prepared.")`
- **Default port depends on version**: `get_address()` returns `port or (8443 if (version == 3 or auto_tls) else 8000)`.
- **Protocol class selection**: `protocol = WebSocketProtocol if self.websocket_enabled else HttpProtocol` when the caller passed none.
- **TLS is forced for HTTP/3**: in `_helper()`, `ssl = process_to_context(ssl)` and then `if version is HTTP.VERSION_3 or auto_tls: ssl = get_ssl_context(self, ssl)` (`sanic/http/tls.py`).
- **Int → enum coercion**: `if isinstance(version, int): version = HTTP(version)`.
- **Config overrides become real config attributes**: `ACCESS_LOG`, `AUTO_RELOAD`, `MOTD`, `NOISY_EXCEPTIONS` are `setattr`-ed onto `self.config` only when explicitly passed.
- **The deployment dict** returned by `_helper()` — `{"protocol", "host", "port", "version", "sock", "unix", "ssl", "app", "signal", "loop", "register_sys_signals", "backlog"}` — is what `Sanic.serve()`/`serve_single()` and `create_server()` consume. `serve_single()` simply calls `worker_serve(monitor_publisher=None, **kwargs)`; `serve()` hands the same kwargs to `WorkerManager(..., worker_serve, kwargs, ...)`, which is how `version` reaches the worker process.

## Stage 3 — the actual fork (`_serve_http_1` / `_serve_http_3`)

`worker_serve()` in [`sanic/worker/serve.py`](https://github.com/sanic-org/sanic/blob/57d44f263fa84bd5cd6f77b5565825640d85b1e2/sanic/worker/serve.py) accepts `version=HTTP.VERSION_1` (alongside `config` / `passthru`) and ends with the switch, after `app.refresh(passthru)`, `app.update_config(config)` and `app.asgi = False`:

```python
if version is HTTP.VERSION_3:
    return _serve_http_3(host, port, app, loop, ssl)
return _serve_http_1(host, port, app, ssl, sock, unix, reuse_port, loop,
                     protocol, backlog, register_sys_signals, run_multiple,
                     run_async, connections, signal, state, asyncio_server_kwargs)
```

Both helpers are defined in [`sanic/server/runners.py`](https://github.com/sanic-org/sanic/blob/57d44f263fa84bd5cd6f77b5565825640d85b1e2/sanic/server/runners.py); `runners.serve()` (the `create_server()` path) takes the same `version` value and makes the same choice, so single-process and multi-worker deployments behave identically:

- **`_serve_http_1`** — TCP path. It builds the protocol factory from the configured protocol class (`HttpProtocol` or `WebSocketProtocol`) injecting `loop`, `connections`, `signal`, `app`, `state`, plus `_build_protocol_kwargs(protocol, app.config)` (which only adds `websocket_max_size` / `websocket_ping_timeout` / `websocket_ping_interval` when the class has a `websocket_handshake`), then calls `loop.create_server(..., host, port, ssl=ssl, sock=sock, unix=unix, reuse_port=reuse_port, backlog=backlog)`, triggers `app._startup()` / server events and returns an `AsyncioServer`.
- **`_serve_http_3`** — QUIC path. It refuses to run when the optional `aioquic` dependency was not importable (raising `ServerError` about HTTP/3 without aioquic), creates a `SessionTicketStore`, obtains the aioquic `QuicConfiguration` from `sanic/http/http3.py::get_config(app, ssl_context)` with the SSL context from `sanic/http/tls.py`, and starts a UDP endpoint through aioquic's `serve(...)` using `Http3Protocol` as the protocol factory. It takes no `protocol`/`backlog`/`sock` arguments — that asymmetry is why HTTP/3 cannot be layered on the TCP socket and why `prepare()` forbids it as a secondary server.

## Stage 4 — protocol objects that carry the version

[`sanic/server/protocols/http_protocol.py`](https://github.com/sanic-org/sanic/blob/57d44f263fa84bd5cd6f77b5565825640d85b1e2/sanic/server/protocols/http_protocol.py) defines the shared `HttpProtocolMixin` (connection setup, `version` property, request/response plumbing that delegates to the `sanic/http/` layer) and two concrete classes:

- `HttpProtocol(HttpProtocolMixin, SanicProtocol)` — `__version__ = HTTP.VERSION_1`, delegating to `sanic.http.Http` (`sanic/http/http1.py`), the asyncio TCP/`Stream` implementation of HTTP/1.1.
- `Http3Protocol(HttpProtocolMixin, ConnectionProtocol)` — `__version__ = HTTP.VERSION_3`, delegating to `sanic.http.Http3` (`sanic/http/http3.py`), driven by aioquic's `QuicConnectionProtocol` callbacks.

So: **`runners.py` decides which socket/server factory runs; the protocol class in `http_protocol.py` + `sanic/http/http1.py|http3.py` decides how bytes are parsed** for that version. Request/response configuration consumed there (timeouts, `REQUEST_MAX_SIZE`, `REQUEST_BUFFER_SIZE`, `ACCESS_LOG`, keep-alive) is read off `app.config` (`sanic/config.py`) at connection/request time, not passed down from the CLI.

## Practical consequences

- To serve HTTP/3 you must supply certificates: `sanic server:app --http 3 --cert fullchain.pem --key privkey.pem` (port defaults to `8443`); HTTP/3 or `--auto-tls` triggers `get_ssl_context()`, and QUIC has no plaintext mode.
- `--http 3` (or `-3`) must come first if you also pass `--http 1`; otherwise `prepare()` raises `RuntimeError`, because only the first prepared instance drives the server-info/socket configuration.
- `pip install sanic[http3]` (aioquic) is required, otherwise startup fails with a `ServerError` rather than silently falling back to HTTP/1.1.
- Everything else (host/port/ssl/backlog/worker count) is still configured in one place — `StartupMixin._helper()` — which normalises values into the deployment dict that both the worker manager and `create_server()` use; `app.config` remains the runtime configuration object the protocol layer reads from.
